summary.headline: Tejas Networks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR406 crores, but PAT stayed at a INR207 crore loss; order book rose to INR2,315 crores on BSNL 4G LOI.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR406 crores in Q2 FY27 versus INR262 crores a year earlier, and H1 revenue reached INR808 crores (about 74% YoY growth). EBITDA was negative INR108 crores (Q1: negative INR99 crores) and PAT was negative INR207 crores (Q2 FY26: negative INR307 crores). Order book rose to INR2,315 crores from INR1,529 crores in Q1, driven by LOI and subsequent POs for the BSNL 4G expansion of 18,000-plus sites. Net working capital fell to INR4,235 crores on lower receivables, while net debt rose to INR4,384 crores from INR4,277 crores as capex and operating costs were funded.

segments.name: Wireless
segments.commentary: Initial RAN and 5G core shipments made for the 18,685-site BSNL LOI; initial shipments of end-to-end 5G network to an international customer in South America began in Q2. Multiple POCs under way in North America and Asia Pacific.

segments.name: Wireline / optical and FTTx
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue driven by optical IP and FTTx shipments to private operators and system integrators. Received POs for GPON FTTx from several Indian ISPs, an LOI from a new SI for IP/MPLS routers for BharatNet middle mile in 3 states, and an order for a pan-India OTN network for a Government of India enterprise.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significant portion of the INR2,314 crore inventory to be consumed in executing the BSNL 4G order over the coming quarters.
Most of the INR1,500 crore BSNL order (LOI from TCS) is expected to convert into POs by end of Q3 FY27; only a substantial portion is in the current order book.
Management expects significant BSNL milestone collections in Q3 FY27, which should substantially reduce receivables, but did not quantify the amount.
Management expects inventory and gross debt to fall significantly as BSNL shipments convert to receivables and collections; no quantified targets given.
Management targets quarterly positive EBITDA and a visible path to profitability in coming years, with no date given.
capex_capacity: Capex continued per plan through Q2, contributing to the rise in net debt.
Developing a compact baseband unit supporting up to 5 frequency bands per site, and expanding 5G radio portfolio across custom bands from 700 MHz to 4.9 GHz.
Expanding IP/MPLS routing portfolio to higher bit rates; developing low-latency access platforms at 200 Gbps and beyond, and terabit-class packet and optical backbone products.
Opened next-generation connectivity lab covering 5G Advanced, 6G and AI-powered network intelligence.
Filed 26 patents in Q2, taking global patent count to 748, of which 266 are 5G Advanced and 6G standards-related.
demand_pricing: Order book INR2,315 crores at Q2-end, 96% India and 4% international; management said the BSNL LOI accounts for only part of the order book and non-BSNL customers contributed the rest.

International traction is in new 5G deployments in emerging markets, where Tejas positions itself as a new, responsive vendor to Tier 1, Tier 2 and smaller operators; several deals are joint solutions with partners such as NEC and Rakuten.
Won a new Tier 1 pan-African operator contract for 400G optical equipment.

Data center interconnect is a focus area, working through system integrators building full data center racks rather than with GPU vendors directly; management cited DCI wins in India and abroad without quantifying them.
Management said Indian private operators had already completed major 4G/5G build-outs, so further Indian mobile wins depend on their next expansion phase.

qa_highlights.question: How much BSNL dues have been recovered and how much is still due, and when will payment come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the milestone delivery requirements have been met and a significant amount of collections linked to those milestones should come in this quarter. It did not give an exact figure but said receivables will fall substantially.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR2,300 crore order book include the INR1,500 crore BSNL order?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a part is in the order book. Purchase orders are issued site by site, and management expects most of the INR1,500 crore to convert by quarter-end. The rest of the order book comes from non-BSNL customers, but no breakdown was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why no wins outside BSNL in India for wireless?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian operators had built their 4G/5G networks already and Tejas must wait for the next expansion phase; qualification through POCs and trials is under way, including with Vi.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company partnering with GPU vendors for AI data centers, and what is the DC stage with TCS?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it partners with system integrators building complete data center racks, and the focus is data center interconnect rather than GPU vendors. No further detail was given on the TCS POC.

qa_highlights.question: What was the INR145 crore contract manufacturing loss in COGS, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision related to the prior year (September 2025) and there is no such provision in Q2 FY27. Management said it was tied to manufacturing for the first 100,000-site order and will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory and gross debt will reduce over 6 to 9 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying inventory should fall significantly over the next few quarters toward levels in line with normal quarterly business, with debt also falling significantly as the order converts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the railways trial and the D2M opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Railways: a 700 MHz 5G network trial section is deployed under a PO, to support internal railway communications and potentially Kavach; expansion depends on results. D2M: Tejas has developed broadcast radio heads and trialled them around Delhi, but will supply as a radio provider to SIs, not as the system integrator.

qa_highlights.question: Is Tejas the exclusive NEC partner, and how does the arrangement work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on NEC's revenue. It said Tejas licensed massive MIMO 5G radio technology from NEC, supplies it to NEC's existing customers and new customers with changes, and is a radio development partner for NEC's future radios.

risks_watch: Inventory of INR2,314 crores and net debt of INR4,384 crores (rising QoQ) must come down as BSNL 4G shipments convert to collections.
BSNL milestone collections are expected in Q3 FY27 but were not quantified; any slippage would affect receivables and cash flow.
EBITDA stayed negative at INR108 crores and PAT at negative INR207 crores; positive quarterly EBITDA is a stated target without a date.
Limited traction with Indian private mobile operators on wireless; international wins are early-stage POCs and depend on qualifying equipment for future expansion phases.
Remaining BSNL LOI (about INR1,500 crores) must convert to POs; management said most is expected by quarter-end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on order book growth, BSNL execution and the international pipeline, but cautious on timing: management declined to quantify BSNL collections, inventory reduction, debt reduction and the TCS-linked PO conversion. It was evasive on the wireless gap in Indian private operators and on NEC revenue.
key_quotes: And this is the quarter when we will see a significant amount of collections coming from BSNL, which are connected to the milestones that we have achieved.
And as a new vendor, we are more suited and more responsive to their needs, right?
And we have to achieve significant inventory reduction based on the execution of this order.
And so the key takeaways for the quarter is that we have a strong growth in order book based on which we have strong business visibility for the next few quarters.

growth.why: Q2 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR406 crore and the order book grew to INR2,315 crore (from INR1,529 crore in Q1), with the BSNL 4G LOI expected to convert to POs by end Q3 FY27, but no revenue growth guidance or company-owned capacity additions were given and EBITDA remains negative with no date for positive EBITDA.
